records.source: וּפְלִשְׁתִּים֙ לָֽקְח֔וּ אֵ֖ת אֲר֣וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיְבִאֻ֛הוּ מֵאֶ֥בֶן הָעֵ֖זֶר אַשְׁדּֽוֹדָה׃
records.gloss: And [the] Philistines took the ark of God, and brought it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.
pieces: Now the Philistines had captured the ark of God, and they brought it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.

L.1: And the Philistines had taken the ark of God, and they brought it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.

R.1: The Philistines had captured the ark of God, the sacred chest. They carried it from Ebenezer to their city of Ashdod.

decisions.choice: had taken: the story picks up again from the battle of 4:11
decisions.reason: The sentence puts the Philistines first, before the verb. This marks a new start that looks back: after the account of Eli's death and the birth of Ichabod (4:12-22), the narrator returns to the capture of the ark told in 4:11 and follows the ark itself.

decisions.choice: the ark of God: the chest that held the covenant tablets and stood for God's presence
decisions.reason: The ark was the gold-covered chest made at Sinai, with the cherubim on its lid (Exodus 25:10-22). Israel had carried it into battle as if it guaranteed victory (4:3-4), and lost it. This chapter shows that the God of the ark was not captured with it.

decisions.choice: from Ebenezer to Ashdod: from Israel's battle camp to a Philistine city
decisions.reason: Ebenezer was where Israel camped before the battle (4:1). Ashdod was one of the five chief cities of the Philistines, near the coast (Joshua 13:3; 6:17 in this book).

decisions.choice: the sacred chest; their city of Ashdod
decisions.reason: Readable explains once what the ark was and that Ashdod was a Philistine city, so that young readers can follow the story.

records.heading: The ark in the temple of Dagon

records.source: וַיִּקְח֤וּ פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ אֶת־אֲר֣וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיָּבִ֥יאוּ אֹת֖וֹ בֵּ֣ית דָּג֑וֹן וַיַּצִּ֥יגוּ אֹת֖וֹ אֵ֥צֶל דָּגֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And took [the] Philistines the ark of God and brought it [into the] house of Dagon, and set it beside Dagon.
pieces: The Philistines took the ark of God, brought it into the temple of Dagon, and set it up beside Dagon.

L.2: And the Philistines took the ark of God and brought it into the house of Dagon, and set it beside Dagon.

R.2: They carried the ark of God into the temple of their god Dagon and set it up next to his statue.

decisions.choice: Dagon: a god the Philistines worshiped
decisions.reason: Dagon had a temple at Gaza as well (Judges 16:23-30). He was worshiped in the region long before the Philistines came, and his name sounds like a common word for grain. Beside Dagon means beside his image in the temple.

decisions.choice: house of Dagon: Dagon's temple
decisions.reason: "House" is the usual word for a god's temple, as with the house of the LORD at Shiloh (1:7, 24).

decisions.choice: setting the ark beside Dagon: a trophy brought before the winning god
decisions.reason: Conquerors often carried the images of defeated peoples into the temple of their own god, to show that their god had won. The Philistines treat the ark this way. The next two mornings show which God is stronger.

decisions.choice: temple (Balanced and Readable); his statue (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "temple" for the house of a god. Readable says "statue" where the Hebrew names Dagon himself, since the ark stood beside his image.

records.source: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֤מוּ אַשְׁדּוֹדִים֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וְהִנֵּ֣ה דָג֗וֹן נֹפֵ֤ל לְפָנָיו֙ אַ֔רְצָה לִפְנֵ֖י אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּקְחוּ֙ אֶת־דָּג֔וֹן וַיָּשִׁ֥בוּ אֹת֖וֹ לִמְקוֹמֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And rose early [the] Ashdodites on [the] next day, and look, Dagon [was] fallen on his face to [the] ground before [the] ark of YHWH; and they took Dagon and returned him to his place.
pieces: When the people of Ashdod got up early the next day, there was Dagon, fallen face down on the ground before the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. So they took Dagon and set him back in his place.

L.3: And the Ashdodites rose early the next day, and look, Dagon had fallen on his face to the ground before the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And they took Dagon and put him back in his place.

R.3: Early the next morning the people of Ashdod found Dagon lying face down on the ground in front of the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They picked Dagon up and put him back where he belonged.

decisions.choice: fallen on his face before the ark: the posture of a worshiper or a defeated servant
decisions.reason: Falling face down to the ground is how a person bows before a greater lord (Joshua 5:14; 1 Samuel 25:23). The god of the winning army lies before the ark of the God whose people lost. The narrator now names the ark "the ark of the LORD", using the divine name as the LORD acts.

decisions.choice: look: what the people of Ashdod saw as they came in
decisions.reason: The word draws the reader into the moment of discovery, seeing the fallen image through the eyes of the people who found it.

decisions.choice: they took Dagon and put him back: the god had to be set up by human hands
decisions.reason: The image could not raise itself. The point is made with a quiet irony that the prophets later make openly (Isaiah 46:7).

decisions.choice: look (Literal); there was (Balanced); found (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the pointing word as "look". Balanced says "there was Dagon", and Readable turns it into the verb "found", which carries the same surprise in plain English.

records.source: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣מוּ בַבֹּקֶר֮ מִֽמָּחֳרָת֒ וְהִנֵּ֣ה דָג֗וֹן נֹפֵ֤ל לְפָנָיו֙ אַ֔רְצָה לִפְנֵ֖י אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֑ה וְרֹ֨אשׁ דָּג֜וֹן וּשְׁתֵּ֣י׀כַּפּ֣וֹת יָדָ֗יו כְּרֻתוֹת֙ אֶל־הַמִּפְתָּ֔ן רַ֥ק דָּג֖וֹן נִשְׁאַ֥ר עָלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And they rose early in [the] morning on [the] next day, and look, Dagon [was] fallen on his face to [the] ground before [the] ark of YHWH, and [the] head of Dagon and [the] two palms of his hands [were] cut off on the threshold; only Dagon was left on him.
pieces: Early the following morning they rose, and there was Dagon, fallen face down on the ground before the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Dagon's head and both his hands lay cut off on the threshold; only his body was left.

L.4: And they rose early in the morning the next day, and look, Dagon had fallen on his face to the ground before the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the head of Dagon and both palms of his hands [were] cut off [and lying] on the threshold. Only Dagon was left of him.

R.4: The next morning they got up early again, and Dagon had fallen face down on the ground in front of the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} once more. This time his head and both his hands had been cut off. They were lying on the threshold of the doorway. Only his body was left.

decisions.choice: head and hands cut off: the marks of an enemy beaten in battle
decisions.reason: Victors cut off the heads or hands of defeated enemies (Judges 8:6; 1 Samuel 17:51; 31:9). Dagon is shown not only bowing but lying like a slain enemy before the ark.

decisions.choice: only Dagon was left: only the trunk of the image remained
alternatives: only Dagon's trunk was left to him
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says, briefly, "only Dagon was left on him". The sense is clear enough: the head and hands were gone and only the body of the statue was left. The wording is unusual, and it may be that a word meaning "body" or "trunk" has dropped out of the text, or that the name stands here for the rest of the figure.

decisions.choice: the threshold: the raised stone at the temple doorway
decisions.reason: The broken pieces lay at the entrance. The next verse explains a custom about this threshold that was still kept when the book was written.

decisions.choice: his body
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what was left, his body, since "only Dagon was left" would not make sense in English after his head and hands are gone.

decisions.choice: again; once more; this time
decisions.reason: Readable adds these small words to show that the same thing happened a second time and was worse, as the repeated wording of verses 3 and 4 shows.

records.source: עַל־כֵּ֡ן לֹֽא־יִדְרְכוּ֩ כֹהֲנֵ֨י דָג֜וֹן וְכָֽל־הַבָּאִ֧ים בֵּית־דָּג֛וֹן עַל־מִפְתַּ֥ן דָּג֖וֹן בְּאַשְׁדּ֑וֹד עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃ס
records.gloss: Therefore not tread [the] priests of Dagon and all those coming [into the] house of Dagon on [the] threshold of Dagon in Ashdod until this day.
pieces: That is why, to this day, the priests of Dagon and everyone who enters Dagon's temple in Ashdod do not step on Dagon's threshold.

L.5: Therefore the priests of Dagon and all who come into the house of Dagon do not tread on the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod, to this day.

R.5: That is why, to this day, Dagon's priests and everyone who goes into his temple in Ashdod do not step on the threshold.

decisions.choice: they do not tread on the threshold: a custom explained by this event
decisions.reason: People entering stepped over the threshold rather than on it, because the broken image had lain there. Zephaniah 1:9 also speaks of people who leap over the threshold, perhaps a practice of the same kind.

decisions.choice: to this day: up to the time the book was written
decisions.reason: The phrase, used here for the first time in 1 Samuel, refers to the writer's own day, when the custom was still kept (also 6:18).

decisions.choice: do not tread: a lasting habit
decisions.reason: The verb describes what is done again and again, a rule kept every time someone enters.

decisions.choice: temple
decisions.reason: As in verse 2, Balanced and Readable say "temple" for Dagon's house.

records.source: וַתִּכְבַּ֧ד יַד־יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־הָאַשְׁדּוֹדִ֖ים וַיְשִׁמֵּ֑ם וַיַּ֤ךְ אֹתָם֙ בַּטְּחֹרִ֔יםאֶת־אַשְׁדּ֖וֹד וְאֶת־גְּבוּלֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And was heavy [the] hand of YHWH on the Ashdodites, and he devastated them and struck them with tumors, Ashdod and its territories.
pieces: Then the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} weighed heavily on the people of Ashdod. He brought ruin on them and struck them with tumors, both Ashdod and the land around it.

L.6: And the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was heavy on the Ashdodites, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} devastated them and struck them with tumors, Ashdod and its territories.

R.6: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} dealt very harshly with the people of Ashdod. He brought disaster on them and struck them with tumors, in the city and in the land around it.

decisions.choice: the hand of the LORD was heavy: the LORD pressed hard on them with his power
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power at work. A heavy hand presses down and punishes. The picture returns in verses 7, 9 and 11, and the Philistines had already feared what this God did to Egypt (4:8).

decisions.choice: devastated them: brought ruin on them
decisions.reason: The verb can mean either to lay waste or to fill with horror. Here it sums up the disaster, which the rest of the verse names.

decisions.choice: tumors: painful swellings, of a kind not known for certain
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) here, in verses 9 and 12 and in 6:4-5 spell *'ofalim*, "swellings" or "mounds", but the scribes marked them to be read aloud as *techorim* (qere), the word used in 6:11 and 6:17. The same pair appears in Deuteronomy 28:27. The reading may have been chosen as a more decent word. Both name a painful lump on the body. Some take them to be hemorrhoids; others take them to be the swellings of a plague, since many people died (verses 11-12) and the Philistines later make gold mice as well as gold tumors (6:4-5). The text does not say which.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew text without the addition in the old Greek translation
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation is longer here: it adds that mice swarmed in the land and there was a great deadly panic in the city. This prepares for the gold mice of 6:4-5, which the Hebrew mentions only there. The Westminster Leningrad Codex, which this translation follows, does not have the addition.

decisions.choice: Ashdod and its territories: the whole area struck, city and surrounding land
decisions.reason: The words follow "them" and spell out who was struck: the city and the villages and fields that belonged to it.

decisions.choice: dealt very harshly with
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of a heavy hand as the LORD dealing harshly with the people.

records.source: וַיִּרְא֥וּ אַנְשֵֽׁי־אַשְׁדּ֖וֹד כִּֽי־כֵ֑ן וְאָמְר֗וּ לֹֽא־יֵשֵׁ֞ב אֲר֨וֹן אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ עִמָּ֔נוּ כִּֽי־קָשְׁתָ֤ה יָדוֹ֙ עָלֵ֔ינוּ וְעַ֖ל דָּג֥וֹן אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: And saw [the] men of Ashdod that [it was] so, and they said, not will stay [the] ark of [the] God of Israel with us, for hard [is] his hand on us and on Dagon our god.
pieces: When the {{gender:people|men}} of Ashdod saw how things stood, they said, "The ark of the God of Israel must not remain among us. His hand is pressing hard on us and on Dagon our god."

L.7: And the men of Ashdod saw that [it was] so, and they said, "The ark of the God of Israel must not stay with us, for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand is hard on us and on Dagon our god."

R.7: The {{gender:people|men}} of Ashdod saw what was happening, and they said, "We cannot keep the ark of the God of Israel here. He is being hard on us and on our god Dagon."

decisions.choice: his hand is hard on us and on Dagon our god: the God of Israel is fighting both the people and their god
decisions.reason: The people of Ashdod see that the disease and the fall of their god have one cause. They name the God of Israel as the one acting, against them and against Dagon, as he had acted against the gods of Egypt (Exodus 12:12; 1 Samuel 4:8).

decisions.choice: must not stay: a decision, not only a prediction
decisions.reason: The verb could be read "will not stay", but in their mouths it is a resolve: the ark has to leave.

decisions.choice: hard: severe, harsh
decisions.reason: This word is close in sense to the "heavy" hand of verse 6; both describe a pressure that will not let up.

decisions.choice: people of Ashdod (default); men of Ashdod (alternative)
decisions.reason: "Men of" a city is the usual way of naming its inhabitants, and the disease struck everyone (verse 9), so Balanced and Readable say "people" by default with "men" as the alternative.

decisions.choice: He is being hard on us
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the hand directly.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלְח֡וּ וַיַּאַסְפוּ֩ אֶת־כָּל־סַרְנֵ֨י פְלִשְׁתִּ֜ים אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ מַֽה־נַּעֲשֶׂ֗ה לַֽאֲרוֹן֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ גַּ֣ת יִסֹּ֔ב אֲר֖וֹן אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיַּסֵּ֕בּוּ אֶת־אֲר֖וֹן אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס
records.gloss: And they sent and gathered all [the] rulers of [the] Philistines to them, and said, what shall we do with [the] ark of [the] God of Israel? And they said, to Gath let go around [the] ark of [the] God of Israel. And they brought around [the] ark of [the] God of Israel.
pieces: So they sent for all the rulers of the Philistines and gathered them together. "What should we do with the ark of the God of Israel?" they asked. The rulers replied, "Have the ark of the God of Israel taken over to Gath." So they took the ark of the God of Israel over there.

L.8: And they sent and gathered all the rulers of the Philistines to themselves, and said, "What shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel?" And they said, "Let the ark of the God of Israel go around to Gath." And they brought the ark of the God of Israel around.

R.8: So they sent for all the Philistine rulers to meet together and asked them, "What should we do with the ark of the God of Israel?" The rulers said, "Move it to Gath." So the ark of Israel's God was moved to Gath.

decisions.choice: the rulers of the Philistines: the lords of the five Philistine cities
decisions.reason: This title is used only for the Philistine leaders. Each of the five cities, Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron, had its own ruler, and they acted together on matters of war and state (Joshua 13:3; 1 Samuel 6:16-18).

decisions.choice: they said: the rulers give the answer
decisions.reason: The Hebrew simply says "they said". Since the question was put to the rulers, the answer is most naturally theirs.

decisions.choice: Gath: another of the five cities, further inland
decisions.reason: Gath lay east of Ashdod, toward the hill country of Judah. It was later the home of Goliath (17:4).

decisions.choice: go around, bring around: move from one place to another
decisions.reason: The verb is used three times in verses 8-10. The ark is passed around from city to city, and the Ekronites use the same word in their complaint (verse 10).

decisions.choice: The rulers replied (Balanced); The rulers said (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speakers, since in English "they said" right after "they asked" would sound like the same people answering themselves.

records.source: וַיְהִ֞י אַחֲרֵ֣י׀הֵסַ֣בּוּ אֹת֗וֹ וַתְּהִ֨י יַד־יְהוָ֤ה׀בָּעִיר֙ מְהוּמָה֙ גְּדוֹלָ֣ה מְאֹ֔ד וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת־אַנְשֵׁ֣י הָעִ֔יר מִקָּטֹ֖ן וְעַד־גָּד֑וֹל וַיִּשָּׂתְר֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם טְחֹרִֽים׃
records.gloss: And it was after they had brought it around, and was [the] hand of YHWH against the city — a panic very great — and he struck [the] men of the city from small and to great, and broke out on them tumors.
pieces: But after they had moved it, the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was against that city and threw it into a great panic. He struck the {{gender:people|men}} of the city, young and old, and tumors broke out on them.

L.9: And after they had brought it around, the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was against the city [with] a very great panic, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} struck the men of the city, from small to great, and tumors broke out on them.

R.9: But after the ark came to Gath, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} turned against that city too, and everyone there panicked. He struck the {{gender:people|men}} of the city, young and old, and they broke out in tumors.

decisions.choice: the hand of the LORD was against the city with a very great panic
decisions.reason: The words "a very great panic" stand beside the clause without a joining word. They describe the form the LORD's hand took: terror and confusion seized the city.

decisions.choice: from small to great: everyone, young and old
decisions.reason: The phrase covers the whole population, from the least to the greatest, whether by age or by rank.

decisions.choice: broke out: the tumors appeared on their bodies
alternatives: the tumors were in their hidden parts
decisions.reason: The verb is found only here. It is usually understood as "burst out" or "broke out". An older understanding takes it from a similar word meaning "hide", so that the tumors were in their hidden parts.

decisions.choice: tumors: as in verse 6
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, the written form is *'ofalim* and the reading marked by the scribes is *techorim*; see the note there on the uncertain kind of swelling.

decisions.choice: people of the city (default); men of the city (alternative)
decisions.reason: As in verse 7, "men of" the city means its inhabitants, young and old, so Balanced and Readable say "people" by default.

decisions.choice: after the ark came to Gath, the LORD turned against that city too
decisions.reason: Readable names the ark and the city, and says "turned against" for the picture of the LORD's hand being against the city.

records.heading: The ark moved from city to city

records.source: וַֽיְשַׁלְּח֛וּ אֶת־אֲר֥וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים עֶקְר֑וֹן וַיְהִ֗י כְּב֨וֹא אֲר֤וֹן הָאֱלֹהִים֙ עֶקְר֔וֹן וַיִּזְעֲק֨וּ הָֽעֶקְרֹנִ֜ים לֵאמֹ֗ר הֵסַ֤בּוּ אֵלַי֙ אֶת־אֲרוֹן֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לַהֲמִיתֵ֖נִי וְאֶת־עַמִּֽי׃
records.gloss: And they sent the ark of God [to] Ekron; and it was, as came [the] ark of God [to] Ekron, then cried out the Ekronites, saying, they have brought around to me [the] ark of [the] God of Israel to kill me and my people.
pieces: So they sent the ark of God on to Ekron. But as soon as the ark of God arrived in Ekron, the people of Ekron cried out, "They have brought the ark of the God of Israel over to us to kill us and our people!"

L.10: And they sent the ark of God to Ekron. And as the ark of God came to Ekron, the Ekronites cried out, saying, "They have brought the ark of the God of Israel around to me, to kill me and my people!"

R.10: Then they sent the ark of God to Ekron. As soon as it arrived, the people of Ekron shouted, "They have brought the ark of Israel's God here to kill us and our people!"

decisions.choice: Ekron: the Philistine city nearest Israel's land
decisions.reason: Ekron lay to the north, on the border of the territory given to Judah (Joshua 15:11). From there the ark would be sent home (6:16).

decisions.choice: me and my people: the city speaks as one
decisions.reason: The Ekronites cry out in the singular, "to me ... to kill me and my people". Each speaks for himself and his people, or the city speaks as one voice.

decisions.choice: they have brought it to kill us: the Ekronites already know what the ark brings
decisions.reason: They do not wait for the disease to arrive. News of Ashdod and Gath has gone before the ark, and they blame those who sent it.

decisions.choice: us, our people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plural for a crowd speaking together; Literal keeps the singular of the Hebrew.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלְח֨וּ וַיַּאַסְפ֜וּ אֶת־כָּל־סַרְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ שַׁלְּח֞וּ אֶת־אֲר֨וֹן אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְיָשֹׁ֣ב לִמְקֹמ֔וֹ וְלֹֽא־יָמִ֥ית אֹתִ֖י וְאֶת־עַמִּ֑י כִּֽי־הָיְתָ֤ה מְהֽוּמַת־מָ֨וֶת֙ בְּכָל־הָעִ֔יר כָּבְדָ֥ה מְאֹ֛ד יַ֥ד הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים שָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And they sent and gathered all [the] rulers of [the] Philistines, and said, send away [the] ark of [the] God of Israel, and let it return to its place, and not will it kill me and my people; for there was a panic of death in all the city; heavy very [was the] hand of God there.
pieces: So they sent for all the rulers of the Philistines and gathered them together. "Send the ark of the God of Israel away," they said. "Let it go back to its own place, so that it does not kill us and our people." For a deadly panic had spread through the whole city; the hand of God was very heavy there.

L.11: And they sent and gathered all the rulers of the Philistines, and said, "Send away the ark of the God of Israel, and let it return to its place, so that it does not kill me and my people." For there was a panic of death in all the city; the hand of God was very heavy there.

R.11: So they called together all the rulers of the Philistines again. "Send the ark of the God of Israel away!" they said. "Let it go back where it belongs, or it will kill us and our people." The whole city was full of panic and death, because God was dealing very harshly with the people there.

decisions.choice: a panic of death: deadly panic
decisions.reason: The panic of verse 9 has now become a panic with death in it: people were dying, and the rest were terrified that they would be next (verse 12).

decisions.choice: the hand of God was very heavy there: the heavy hand that began in verse 6
decisions.reason: The "heavy hand" closes the story of the ark's journey through Philistia (verses 6, 7, 9). The word "heavy" belongs to the same family as the word "glory": Ichabod's name said that the glory had gone from Israel (4:21-22), yet God's weight now presses on the land that took the ark.

decisions.choice: let it return ... so that it does not kill: the purpose of sending it away
decisions.reason: The requests are linked: send it home, so that it will stop killing. As in verse 10 the people speak in the singular, "me and my people".

decisions.choice: us, our people
decisions.reason: As in verse 10, Balanced and Readable use the plural for the crowd.

decisions.choice: again; God was dealing very harshly with the people
decisions.reason: Readable adds "again" because the rulers were called a second time (verse 8), and explains the heavy hand as in verse 6.

records.source: וְהָֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־מֵ֔תוּ הֻכּ֖וּ בַּטְּחֹרִ֑יםוַתַּ֛עַל שַֽׁוְעַ֥ת הָעִ֖יר הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And the men who not died were struck with tumors, and went up [the] cry of the city [to] the heavens.
pieces: Those who did not die were struck with tumors, and the cry of the city for help rose up to heaven.

L.12: And the men who did not die were struck with tumors, and the cry of the city went up to the heavens.

R.12: Those who did not die had tumors. The people of the city cried out for help, and their cry went up to heaven.

decisions.choice: the cry of the city: a cry for help in distress
decisions.reason: The word is used for a desperate call for rescue. It recalls Israel in Egypt, whose cry for help went up to God (Exodus 2:23), but now it is the Philistines who cry out.

decisions.choice: tumors: as in verse 6
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, the written form is *'ofalim* and the reading marked by the scribes is *techorim*.

decisions.choice: went up to the heavens: a loud and desperate cry
decisions.reason: The cry rose high into the sky, so loud and so great was the distress.

decisions.choice: Those who
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the men", meaning the people of the city who survived, so Balanced and Readable say "those", which includes everyone.
